#### 1. acromesomelic dysplasia 2A  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.744)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2129379)

**Proposed mechanism:** GDF5 (HGNC:4220) —DISRUPTS→ Bone Morphogenetic Protein signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); Bone Morphogenetic Protein signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Short fingers (HP:0001328); Bone Morphogenetic Protein signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Short foot (HP:0001762); Bone Morphogenetic Protein signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormalities of the long bones (HP:0002710). Disruption of the GDF5 gene leads to dysregulation of the Bone Morphogenetic Protein signaling pathway, which in turn causes a spectrum of skeletal abnormalities including short fingers, short feet, and general long bone abnormalities, manifesting as brachydactyly type C and acromesomelic dysplasia 2A.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in GDF5 associated with loss-of-function in one disease and gain-of-function in the other, or the absence of GDF5 as a causal gene for either disease. _(variant: rs143331724)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GDF5 in these skeletal dysplasias could enable the development of targeted therapies that modulate BMP signaling to correct bone development defects in both conditions.
